subject: IPv6, MTU, and SDN egress attestation for Private VPC handoff
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: NetOps (Acme) <netops@acme.com>, alex.telco@edgeconnect.net
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: IPv6, MTU, and SDN egress attestation for Private VPC handoff

Hi team —

We're preparing the final handoff for Acme Financial's Private VPC. Two items came up during staging that we need to lock down for compliance and the on-prem runbook:

1) IPv6 traffic handling for cross-site egress (customer requires native IPv6 path or verifiable NAT64 translation).
2) End-to-end MTU (we observed path MTU drops when enabling jumbo frames; need confirmation that 9000 will be tolerated across the egress path).

Irene / Ben — can you provide the SDN overlay choice and specifics on how egress is anchored (SNAT vs routed egress gateway) and attach the tests/evidence we ran in staging? Acme's security team is asking for an attestation PDF that we can sign off on (format in the attachment template).

Attachments: vpc-sdn-diagram-v3.png (reference), ipv6-attestation-template.docx (template)

Goal: Provide a short attestation PDF and MTU test CSV by EOD Tuesday so Acme can file it for their audit.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: NetOps (Acme) <netops@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, alex.telco@edgeconnect.net
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: IPv6, MTU, and SDN egress attestation for Private VPC handoff

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side before we accept the attestation: 

- For IPv6, can you confirm whether the VPC egress will use EUI-64-based addressing or an assigned ULA/RFC4193 range for tenant traffic? We need to ensure no address overlap with our peered services.
- For MTU: our edge boxes are currently set to 9216; if you advertise 9000 we should be fine, but we need a path MTU log showing no ICMP-blackhole results when transmitting 8k and 12k frames (for our verification).

Also, Alex from EdgeConnect copied in for the SDN overlay behavior — if you intend to terminate the overlay at our border and do SNAT there, we'll need the egress gateway's ASN and a simple BGP session plan (ASN, prefix announcement expectations).

Appreciate the artifacts. We can accept an attestation signed by Redwood's Ops lead plus a short test report.

—NetOps (Acme)
netops@acme.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: NetOps (Acme) <netops@acme.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: IPv6, MTU, and SDN egress attestation for Private VPC handoff

NetOps / Karthik —

Summary of technical approach (staging results attached):

- SDN overlay: We used an EVPN-VXLAN fabric (OVS-based forwarding plane) inside the private pod. That simplifies tenant addressing and preserves IPv6 headers end-to-end; we do NOT rewrite IPv6 unless forced by edge NAT policy.

- IPv6 addressing: We provisioned a customer ULA block (fd:acme:100::/48) inside the VPC. The edge NAT64 path is available as a fallback but is only enabled if the peer signals lacking IPv6 reachability. The ULA avoids public global allocation conflicts with Acme's announced space.

- Egress anchoring: By default we terminate the overlay at the on-prem border devices and perform a routed handoff to Acme's edge via BGP (no SNAT on the Redwood side for IPv6). For IPv4, we have an option to SNAT at the egress gateway (configured via canary toggle).

- MTU testing: Attached is mtu-path-scan-20261221.csv. Test summary: 8192-byte UDP probe -> successful end-to-end when jumbo is enabled on both sides; 12288-byte probe -> fragmented/ICMP required on 2/12 test hops in the path during peak. Our recommendation: advertise 9000 but include an operational note to monitor DF/PMTU logs for the first 72 hours of production. We also baked a fallback to 1500 on the egress gateway in case we observe consistent PMTU blackholes.

Attachments: mtu-path-scan-20261221.csv, vpc-sdn-diagram-v3.png

Commands / logs (redacted):
- iperf3 -c acme-edge -M 8192 -> MSS 8168, successful
- tracepath -n acme-egress | grep mtu -> hop 7 reported mtu 1500 at 2026-12-21T03:12Z (intermittent)

Next steps:
- We will produce an attestation PDF (ipv6-egress-attestation.pdf) that states: "Native IPv6 routing supported; ULA allocation used; MTU 9000 recommended with 1500 fallback; monitoring guardrails enabled."
- Ben to add BGP session parameters (ASN/prefixes) and sign the attestation as Ops lead.

Thanks,
Irene
Sr. Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: NetOps (Acme) <netops@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: IPv6, MTU, and SDN egress attestation for Private VPC handoff

NetOps / Alex —

Thanks for the review and callouts. Attached is the completed attestation (ipv6-egress-attestation.pdf) and the MTU scan CSV we ran last week. Key decisions we are asking Acme to accept before cutover: 

- Accept fd:acme:100::/48 as the tenant ULA for internal addressing. This avoids any overlap and keeps global BGP announcements under Acme's control.
- Accept recommended MTU=9000 with the documented 1500 fallback and 72-hour DF/PMTU monitoring window. We'll provide the alert hooks to Acme's SRE (Ops playbook link below).
- BGP details: ASN 65055 (Redwood egress gateway) will peer with Acme's ASN 65532; Redwood will advertise only the tenant aggregate 10.100.0.0/16 (IPv4) and fd:acme:100::/48 (IPv6) from the on-prem border.

If these bullets are acceptable, please reply with an approval email that we can store with the attestation for your compliance team. Ben, can you paste the small BGP snippet into the PDF (snippet attached) and add your signature?

Related links: https://drive.reddemo.com/shared/vpc-sdn/v3 (runbook + diagrams)

Thanks and happy holidays,
Marissa Cole
Head of Deployments
Redwood Inference
